decision.detail: I don't turn around when Larry's bag hits the doorframe. I don't ask about his reel. I walk to the patch, the one with my recording already threaded into it, and I put my hand on the line-switch. Station line to Pittsburgh. I click it over. I keep the levels where they are. No title card. No slug. No producer's voice saying *this is an interview with*. Just Alma. Forty-two winters of her hands on the projector arm, her voice saying whatever she said to the machine and the dark and the daughter she's been promising this to. I watch the line-light go steady. I don't add a sign-off. I let her last sentence end in the air and hold the transmit until the tail of it clears the line, then I click it back. The patch hums. The booth is quiet. I sit down in the chair I dragged over for her bad back, and I don't get up.
decision.intention: One voice to one daughter before the reels stop turning. No package. No credit. No second take. The line is open now and it will not be open in a week. She made the promise. I made the recording. I send it. That is the whole job.
decision.words: You go, Larry. Pittsburgh gets a voice tonight.

messages.content: You are Rita Hanson, a TV producer. You want to make your own piece. Alma, who ran the Rialto projectors for 42 winters, promised her daughter in Pittsburgh an interview. Cover the festival or spend the evening as you choose. Pick an immediate physical act you can carry out, optional words and a practical intention. Your words do not make anyone else act. Silence is allowed. You may refuse, tell a lie, or leave without explaining yourself.
